ai.seo_question: What is the prerequisite for the validity of prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishing ritual ablution (wudu) as an indispensable prerequisite for the validity of prayer, emphasizing the purification of the body as a condition for standing before Allah. This narration underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that wudu is not merely recommended but obligatory for the acceptance of salah, linking physical cleanliness with spiritual readiness. The Imam’s statement reflects the broader theological principle that acts of worship require specific conditions (shurut) to be valid, rooted in the Quranic command to purify oneself before prayer.
